note: Agricultural Science round 1 (part B): animal production (classification/terminology, anatomy and physiology, reproduction, nutrition, management, health, fisheries/wildlife/bees), agricultural economics and extension (factors of production, economic principles, farm management and records, marketing, extension) and agricultural technology (surveying and farmstead planning, simple tools, machinery and mechanisation, processing and storage, biotechnology/ICT/research) - with a broiler enterprise record, a pig ration table, a tomato demand schedule and a farm survey case as passages.

passages.title: Bola's broiler cycle
passages.text:
Bola raised 500 day-old broiler chicks for
8 weeks. Her records show:

Item                    Amount (₦)
Day-old chicks           250,000
Feed                     900,000
Drugs and vaccines        50,000
Labour                   100,000
Depreciation of pens      20,000

Mortality was 4%. She sold all the
surviving birds at ₦4,500 each.

passages.title: Ration for weaner pigs
passages.text:
A farmer mixes a ration for weaner pigs
from the ingredients below.

Ingredient        Qty (kg)   Protein
Maize                60        9%
Soya bean meal       25       44%
Wheat offal          12       15%
Premix and salt       3        0%
Total               100

passages.title: Demand for tomatoes at Mile 12 market
passages.text:
The table shows the quantity of tomatoes
demanded at Mile 12 market at different
prices.

Price per basket (₦)   Baskets demanded
10,000                       500
8,000                        700
6,000                      1,000
4,000                      1,500

During the dry season the harvest falls
and few baskets reach the market.

passages.title: Laying out Chidi's farm
passages.text: Chidi wants to measure and map his rectangular farm before building a poultry house. Using a measuring tape, ranging poles, pegs and a prismatic compass, he finds the farm measures 120 m by 80 m. He plans to site the poultry house at the far end from the road, downwind of the farmhouse, with a water tank nearby and a farm road linking all the buildings.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The total cost of production for Bola's broiler cycle was

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The number of birds Bola sold was
questions.explanation: 4% of 500 = 20 birds died; 500 − 20 = 480 birds sold.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Bola's total revenue from the cycle was

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Bola's profit for the cycle was
questions.explanation: Profit = revenue − total cost = 2,160,000 − 1,320,000 = ₦840,000.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Feed accounted for what percentage of Bola's total cost, to the nearest whole number?
questions.explanation: 900,000 ÷ 1,320,000 × 100 ≈ 68%. Feed is normally the largest cost in poultry production.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The cost of producing one bird sold (average cost) was
questions.explanation: ₦1,320,000 ÷ 480 birds = ₦2,750 per bird sold.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Depreciation of the pens is classified as a
questions.explanation: Fixed costs (depreciation, rent, interest) do not change with the number of birds; feed, chicks and drugs are variable costs.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: If Bola had reduced mortality to zero, her profit would have increased by
questions.explanation: 20 more birds × ₦4,500 = ₦90,000 extra revenue (costs are already incurred).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The crude protein contributed by the maize in the ration is
questions.explanation: 60 kg × 9% = 5.4 kg of crude protein.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The crude protein contributed by the soya bean meal is
questions.explanation: 25 kg × 44% = 11 kg of crude protein from the soya bean meal.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The crude protein content of the whole 100 kg ration is

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The ingredient that serves mainly as the energy source in the ration is
questions.explanation: Cereals such as maize supply carbohydrate energy; soya bean meal supplies protein.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The premix in the ration supplies
questions.explanation: Premixes are concentrated mixtures of vitamins and micro-minerals added in small amounts.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which ingredient could replace soya bean meal as a protein source?
questions.explanation: Groundnut cake, fish meal, blood meal and cottonseed cake are protein concentrates.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The table illustrates the law of
questions.explanation: As price falls, the quantity demanded rises, other things being equal: the law of demand.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: If the price falls from ₦8,000 to ₦6,000 per basket, the quantity demanded increases by

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The total amount spent by buyers when the price is ₦6,000 per basket is

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: During the dry season, with demand unchanged and supply reduced, the price of tomatoes would be expected to
questions.explanation: A leftward shift of the supply curve with the same demand raises the equilibrium price; this is the seasonal price rise farmers exploit with irrigation.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: If a demand curve is drawn from the table, it will slope
questions.explanation: Price and quantity demanded move in opposite directions, giving a downward-sloping demand curve.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Between ₦10,000 and ₦8,000, the percentage change in quantity demanded is 40% for a 20% fall in price. Demand over this range is
questions.explanation: Elasticity = 40 ÷ 20 = 2, greater than 1, so demand is elastic.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The area of Chidi's farm is
questions.explanation: 120 m × 80 m = 9,600 m², slightly less than one hectare (10,000 m²).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The instrument Chidi used to determine the bearings of the farm boundaries is the
questions.explanation: The prismatic compass measures bearings; the tape measures distances; poles and pegs mark points.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The perimeter of the farm, which Chidi must fence, is

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Siting the poultry house downwind of the farmhouse is intended to
questions.A: keep the birds warm during the harmattan season
questions.B: reduce the cost of feeding and watering the birds
questions.C: stop odours and dust blowing towards the dwelling
questions.D: attract customers who pass along the farm road
questions.explanation: Farmstead planning considers wind direction, drainage, accessibility and distance between buildings.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a principle of farmstead planning illustrated in the passage?
questions.A: buildings should be scattered at random over the farm
questions.B: farm roads are unnecessary on a farm of this size
questions.C: livestock houses should be built inside the farmhouse
questions.D: easy access between buildings and a nearby water supply
questions.explanation: Good layout saves labour, improves hygiene and allows expansion.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: If Chidi draws his farm to a scale of 1:1,000, the length of the farm on the map will be

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: Farm animals that chew the cud and have a four-chambered stomach are called
questions.explanation: Cattle, sheep and goats are ruminants; pigs and poultry are monogastric (simple-stomached).

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: A young female pig that has not yet farrowed is called a
questions.explanation: Sow = adult female; boar = adult male; barrow = castrated male; piglet = young.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The act of giving birth in sheep is called
questions.explanation: Cattle calve, goats kid, pigs farrow, horses foal and rabbits kindle.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: A castrated male cattle used for draught work is called
questions.explanation: Castration makes the animal docile; a heifer is a young female that has not calved.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: A young female fowl before it starts laying is called a
questions.explanation: Cockerel = young male; capon = castrated male; hen = laying female.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: Which of the following breeds of cattle is indigenous to Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Indigenous breeds include White Fulani, Sokoto Gudali, Red Bororo, N'dama, Muturu and Keteku.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The N'dama and Muturu breeds are valued in the forest zone because they are
questions.explanation: These humpless breeds resist trypanosomiasis carried by tsetse fly.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: Which of the following is an exotic dairy breed of cattle?
questions.explanation: Friesian and Jersey are dairy breeds; Hereford and Aberdeen Angus are beef breeds.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The West African Dwarf goat is
questions.A: found in the northern savanna and used for milk
questions.B: the largest goat breed in Africa
questions.C: an exotic breed imported from Europe
questions.D: a small trypano-tolerant breed of the humid south
questions.explanation: Northern breeds include the Sokoto Red (Maradi) and Sahel goats.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: Which of the following breeds of sheep is Nigerian?
questions.explanation: Nigerian breeds are Yankasa, Uda, Balami and West African Dwarf; Merino is an Australian wool breed.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The Large White and Landrace are breeds of
questions.explanation: Exotic pig breeds include Large White, Landrace, Duroc and Hampshire.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: A male goat is called a
questions.explanation: Female goat = doe (nanny), young = kid; male sheep = ram, female = ewe.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: Poultry is a term that covers
questions.A: all the animals kept on a farm
questions.B: fish, snails and bees kept on a farm
questions.C: cattle, sheep and goats kept for meat
questions.D: domesticated birds such as fowls, ducks and turkeys
questions.explanation: Poultry are kept for meat and eggs.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: Animals such as horses and rabbits digest fibre mainly in the caecum and are described as
questions.B: carnivores that feed on flesh only
questions.D: omnivores that eat both plants and flesh
questions.explanation: They have a simple stomach but a large caecum where microbes ferment cellulose.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Classification and Terminology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The meat of goat and sheep are respectively called
questions.explanation: Beef = cattle, pork = pig, veal = calf, lamb = young sheep, venison = deer.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The four compartments of the ruminant stomach are the
questions.D: liver, pancreas, gall bladder and spleen
questions.explanation: Microbes in the rumen digest cellulose; the abomasum is the true glandular stomach.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: In the ruminant stomach, the true (glandular) stomach where enzymes act is the
questions.explanation: The abomasum secretes acid and pepsin like the stomach of monogastric animals.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: Micro-organisms in the rumen enable cattle to
questions.A: digest cellulose and synthesise microbial protein
questions.C: lay eggs during the rainy season
questions.D: digest bone and other hard materials
questions.explanation: Rumen microbes ferment fibre to volatile fatty acids and convert non-protein nitrogen such as urea into protein.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: In the fowl, food is stored and softened in the
questions.explanation: The crop stores food; the proventriculus secretes enzymes; the gizzard grinds food with grit.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The organ of the fowl that grinds food, replacing the function of teeth, is the
questions.explanation: Grit in the muscular gizzard helps grind grains.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The common opening in birds through which faeces, urine and eggs pass is the
questions.explanation: The cloaca opens to the outside through the vent.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The udder of a cow is made up of
questions.C: four quarters each with a teat
questions.explanation: Each quarter is independent; mastitis may affect one quarter only.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The hormone that stimulates milk let-down in the dairy cow is
questions.explanation: Oxytocin is released when the calf suckles or the udder is washed; adrenaline (fear) blocks let-down.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The part of the digestive system where most absorption of digested food takes place is the
questions.explanation: Villi in the small intestine absorb nutrients into the blood and lymph.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The circulatory system of farm animals transports
questions.A: nutrients, oxygen, hormones and waste products
questions.B: sound from the ears to the brain
questions.C: light from the eyes to the brain
questions.D: food from the mouth to the crop
questions.explanation: The heart pumps blood through arteries, capillaries and veins.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The enzyme in the stomach of pigs that begins protein digestion is
questions.explanation: Pepsin works in acid conditions; amylase digests starch and lipase digests fats.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: A cow's rumen is described as a fermentation vat because
questions.A: it secretes hydrochloric acid and pepsin
questions.B: it grinds food in the way a gizzard does
questions.C: anaerobic microbes break down fibre there to fatty acids
questions.D: it absorbs water and minerals only
questions.explanation: The gases (methane and carbon dioxide) are removed by belching; failure to belch causes bloat.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The skeleton of farm animals functions to
questions.A: produce milk and store it for the young
questions.B: regulate body temperature during the day
questions.C: digest food and absorb the nutrients
questions.D: support the body, protect organs and permit movement
questions.explanation: Bone marrow produces red blood cells; bones also store calcium and phosphorus.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: Which of the following organs removes nitrogenous waste from the blood of farm animals?
questions.explanation: The kidneys filter urea from the blood to form urine.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.topic: Anatomy and Physiology of Farm Animals
questions.q: The excretory product of birds, passed out with faeces as a white paste, is
questions.explanation: Birds excrete uric acid, which conserves water.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The period during which a female animal will accept the male is called
questions.explanation: Signs of heat in cattle include restlessness, mounting other cows, mucus discharge and standing to be mounted.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The gestation period of a cow is about
questions.explanation: Cow 280–285 days; sow 114 days; ewe and doe about 150 days; rabbit 31 days.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The gestation period of a sow is approximately
questions.B: 283 days, the same as a cow
questions.C: 150 days, the same as a goat
questions.D: 31 days, the same as a rabbit
questions.explanation: Pigs farrow about 114 days after mating.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The gestation period of goats and sheep is about
questions.explanation: Both kid and lamb after roughly five months.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The oestrous cycle of a cow lasts about
questions.explanation: If not pregnant, the cow returns to heat every 18–24 days; heat itself lasts 12–18 hours.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The male reproductive cells are produced in the
questions.explanation: The scrotum holds the testes outside the body, keeping them cooler for sperm production.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: In the female animal, fertilisation normally takes place in the
questions.explanation: The fertilised egg then moves to the uterus where it implants.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The hormone produced by the ovary that prepares the uterus for pregnancy and maintains it is
questions.explanation: Oestrogen causes heat signs; progesterone from the corpus luteum maintains pregnancy.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The period from the birth of a calf until the cow is dried off is called
questions.explanation: Lactation in dairy cows lasts about 305 days followed by a 60-day dry period.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Weaning is the
questions.A: birth of young animals after gestation
questions.C: mating of the female with the male
questions.D: gradual change of the young from milk to solid feed
questions.explanation: Piglets are weaned at 4–6 weeks, calves at 3–6 months and lambs at 3–4 months.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: In poultry, the incubation period of a chicken egg is
questions.explanation: Ducks take 28 days and turkeys 28 days; guinea fowl 26–28 days.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of artificial insemination?
questions.A: it spreads venereal diseases in the herd
questions.B: it is impossible to carry out in cattle
questions.C: it requires no skill or special equipment
questions.D: one superior sire can serve many females far apart
questions.explanation: AI also allows the use of semen from bulls in other countries and reduces the cost of keeping bulls.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A farmer noticed his cow on heat on 1 March and had her inseminated. If conception occurred, the expected calving date is about
questions.explanation: 283 days from 1 March falls around 9 December; count 9 months and about a week.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The colostrum produced by a cow in the first days after calving is important because it
questions.A: is low in nutrients and easy to digest
questions.B: is meant only for the farmer's household
questions.C: is poisonous to the calf if drunk too early
questions.D: contains antibodies that protect the calf from disease
questions.explanation: Calves should suckle colostrum within six hours of birth to absorb the antibodies.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Egg formation in the hen takes place in the
questions.explanation: The yolk is released from the ovary and receives albumen, membranes and shell as it passes down the oviduct in about 25 hours.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The age at which farm animals become sexually mature is called
questions.explanation: Puberty is reached at about 6–8 months in pigs, 12–18 months in local cattle and 20–24 weeks in layers.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A ration that contains all the nutrients in the right proportions for an animal's needs is described as
questions.explanation: A balanced ration supplies carbohydrates, proteins, fats, minerals, vitamins and water in correct amounts.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Feeds such as grass, hay and silage that are high in fibre and bulky are called
questions.explanation: Roughages are the main feed of ruminants; concentrates (grains, cakes) are low in fibre and high in energy or protein.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a protein concentrate?
questions.explanation: Groundnut cake, soya bean meal, fish meal and blood meal supply protein; maize and molasses supply energy.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The nutrient that supplies most of the energy in livestock feeds is
questions.explanation: Cereals and their by-products are the main carbohydrate (energy) sources.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The class of nutrients needed for growth, repair of tissues and milk production is
questions.explanation: Proteins are made of amino acids; young and lactating animals need the most.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A maintenance ration is one that
questions.A: supports rapid growth and heavy milk production
questions.B: is fed only to sick animals under treatment
questions.C: fattens the animal quickly before it is sold
questions.D: keeps the animal alive with no gain or loss in weight
questions.explanation: Production rations provide extra nutrients above maintenance for growth, milk, eggs or work.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Calcium and phosphorus are required by laying hens mainly for
questions.A: colour of the feathers and comb
questions.B: digestion of fibre in the gizzard
questions.D: vision in the dark and at night
questions.explanation: Oyster shell and bone meal are common calcium and phosphorus supplements.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Deficiency of vitamin A in poultry leads to
questions.C: scaly legs and loss of feathers
questions.D: poor vision, poor growth and low resistance
questions.explanation: Yellow maize and green leaves supply vitamin A precursors.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Rickets in young animals is caused by deficiency of
questions.B: iron and copper in the diet
questions.explanation: Rickets shows as soft, bent bones; sunlight helps animals make vitamin D.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Anaemia in piglets kept indoors is prevented by giving
questions.explanation: Sow's milk is low in iron; piglets with no access to soil need iron in the first days of life.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Urea can be fed to ruminants but not to poultry because
questions.A: poultry dislike the taste and refuse the feed
questions.B: poultry do not need any protein in their feed
questions.C: urea is a vitamin needed only by cattle
questions.D: rumen microbes turn urea into protein; poultry cannot
questions.explanation: Non-protein nitrogen is useful only where microbial fermentation precedes enzymatic digestion.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The feed conversion ratio (FCR) of a broiler that consumed 4 kg of feed and gained 2 kg live weight is
questions.explanation: FCR = feed consumed ÷ weight gain = 4 ÷ 2 = 2.0; a lower FCR means more efficient conversion.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Using Pearson's square, the proportions of maize (9% CP) and soya bean meal (44% CP) needed to make a 16% CP ration are
questions.A: 28 parts maize to 7 parts soya bean meal
questions.B: 7 parts maize to 28 parts soya bean meal
questions.D: 16 parts maize to 9 parts soya bean meal
questions.explanation: Differences from 16: soya 44 − 16 = 28 (parts of maize); 16 − 9 = 7 (parts of soya). 28 : 7 = 80% maize, 20% soya.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Water is essential to farm animals because it
questions.A: supplies most of the energy they need
questions.B: is the main vitamin in the animal's diet
questions.C: supplies the protein needed for growth
questions.D: regulates body temperature and transports nutrients
questions.explanation: A dairy cow may drink over 60 litres a day; water shortage reduces feed intake and production.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Feed additives such as antibiotics and coccidiostats are included in rations to
questions.B: replace the protein in the ration
questions.D: give the feed a bright colour
questions.explanation: Additives are used in small quantities; overuse of antibiotics causes resistance.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The main by-product of the brewing industry used as livestock feed is
questions.explanation: Brewers' grains are a good source of protein and fibre for cattle and pigs.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following mineral elements is needed for haemoglobin formation?
questions.explanation: Iron deficiency causes anaemia; iodine deficiency causes goitre; calcium deficiency causes rickets and milk fever.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A farmer fed his layers a ration low in calcium. The most likely result is
questions.A: an increase in the number of eggs laid
questions.B: brightly coloured yolks in the eggs
questions.D: thin-shelled or shell-less eggs and fewer eggs
questions.explanation: Each egg-shell needs about 2 g of calcium; layers' mash should contain 3–4% calcium.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The system of poultry keeping in which birds are confined in wire cages with feed and water provided is the
questions.explanation: Battery cages ease egg collection and disease control but need high capital and restrict the birds.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: In the deep litter system of poultry keeping, the floor is covered with
questions.B: wire mesh raised above the ground
questions.D: wood shavings, sawdust or chopped straw
questions.explanation: Litter absorbs droppings and must be kept dry to prevent disease and ammonia build-up.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The extensive system of livestock production is characterised by
questions.B: the use of battery cages for the birds
questions.C: animals roaming freely over wide areas with few inputs
questions.D: zero grazing with fodder carried to the animals
questions.explanation: Nomadic cattle rearing and free-range village poultry are extensive systems.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The intensive system of livestock management differs from the extensive system in that it
questions.A: requires much less capital to set up
questions.B: produces a lower output per animal
questions.C: needs a much larger area of land
questions.D: confines the animals and provides all their feed
questions.explanation: Intensive systems give higher output per animal but cost more and risk rapid disease spread.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Brooding of day-old chicks involves
questions.A: giving chicks warmth, feed, water and protection
questions.B: vaccinating the adult birds against disease
questions.C: collecting eggs from the laying boxes
questions.D: slaughtering the old hens for sale
questions.explanation: Chicks cannot regulate their temperature; brooder temperature starts at about 35 °C and is reduced weekly.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Debeaking (beak trimming) is carried out in poultry to prevent
questions.explanation: Overcrowding, bright light and nutrient deficiency encourage pecking.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Castration of male farm animals is done to
questions.B: increase the milk yield of the herd
questions.C: improve their performance as breeding sires
questions.D: make them docile and improve fattening and meat
questions.explanation: Methods include the burdizzo, rubber ring (elastrator) and open (surgical) method.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Dehorning of calves is carried out to
questions.A: increase the size of the horns later
questions.B: improve the milk yield of the cows
questions.C: prevent injury to other animals and handlers
questions.explanation: Hot iron or caustic paste is applied to the horn buds of young calves.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Culling in a poultry flock means
questions.A: buying new birds to add to the flock
questions.B: moving the birds to a new poultry house
questions.C: vaccinating all the birds in the flock
questions.D: removing unproductive, sick or deformed birds
questions.explanation: Culling saves feed and reduces disease spread.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a good practice in housing pigs?
questions.A: providing no water in the pens
questions.B: keeping the pigs in battery cages
questions.C: cool, well-ventilated pens with a wallow or sprinkler
questions.D: housing the pigs together with the poultry
questions.explanation: Pigs have few sweat glands and need help to keep cool.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Ear notching and tattooing in pigs and cattle are methods of
questions.explanation: Identification allows accurate records of breeding, health and performance.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Keeping farm records helps the livestock farmer to
questions.A: increase the spread of disease in the herd
questions.B: avoid selling any of the animals
questions.C: assess performance and detect problems early
questions.D: reduce the feed given to the animals to zero
questions.explanation: Records include production, feed, health, breeding and financial records.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A layer farm records 800 eggs per day from 1,000 hens. The hen-day egg production percentage is
questions.explanation: 800 ÷ 1,000 × 100 = 80%; commercial layers peak at 90% or more.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Rabbits are housed in
questions.explanation: Pigs are kept in sties (pens), cattle in byres or kraals, poultry in coops or pens.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Dipping or spraying of cattle is carried out to control
questions.explanation: Acaricides kill ticks, which transmit diseases such as babesiosis and heart-water.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The main aim of the fold system of poultry keeping is to
questions.B: keep the birds in cages above the ground
questions.C: raise broilers for the Christmas market
questions.D: move the birds over fresh pasture in a portable fold
questions.explanation: Folds are moved each day to prevent build-up of parasites.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following causes stress and lowers production in poultry?
questions.B: clean water supplied at all times
questions.C: overcrowding, heat and sudden changes in feed
questions.D: correct lighting in the poultry house
questions.explanation: Stressed birds eat less, lay fewer eggs and are more prone to disease.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A disease that spreads from one animal to another is described as
questions.explanation: Contagious diseases are caused by pathogens: viruses, bacteria, protozoa, fungi and parasites.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Newcastle disease of poultry is caused by a
questions.explanation: Newcastle disease causes twisted necks, greenish diarrhoea and high mortality; it is controlled by vaccination.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Wildlife conservation is important because it

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The four factors of production are
questions.A: land, labour, capital and the entrepreneur
questions.B: rain, sunshine, soil and improved seed
questions.C: money, banks, roads and market stalls
questions.D: crops, animals, fish and forest trees
questions.explanation: Their rewards are rent, wages, interest and profit respectively.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.explanation: Labour earns wages, capital earns interest and the entrepreneur earns profit.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.C: the members of the farmer's household

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.explanation: The farm manager decides what, how and how much to produce and takes the profit or loss.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Land as a factor of production is unique because it is
questions.A: fixed in supply and a free gift of nature
questions.B: mobile and can be moved to a new site
questions.explanation: Land includes soil, water, minerals, forests and climate.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.B: must be paid at the end of every day

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Marginal product is the

questions.C: average output per unit of input used
questions.D: extra output from one more unit of input
questions.explanation: Marginal product = change in total product ÷ change in input.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Demand for a product is described as elastic when

questions.B: the product is a necessity such as garri
questions.C: a small price change causes a larger change in quantity
questions.D: price and quantity move in the same direction
questions.explanation: Luxuries and goods with close substitutes have elastic demand; staple foods tend to be inelastic.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.C: the total cost of producing the crop
questions.D: the cost of transporting produce to market
questions.explanation: If a farmer uses land for maize instead of cassava, the cassava income forgone is the opportunity cost.

questions.explanation: The manager decides what to produce, how much and by what method.

questions.C: a list of the workers employed on the farm

questions.B: only the sales made by the farm
questions.C: only the purchases made by the farm
questions.D: the assets and liabilities of the farm

questions.explanation: Fixed costs such as rent and depreciation are incurred even when nothing is produced.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A farm budget is

questions.B: a list of the animals on the farm
questions.C: a plan of expected income and expenses ahead
questions.D: a test of the fertility of the soil
questions.explanation: Budgets help the farmer to choose between enterprises and to obtain credit.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A farmer's inventory shows assets of ₦5,000,000 and liabilities of ₦1,500,000 at the start of the year, and assets of ₦6,200,000 and liabilities of ₦1,200,000 at the end. The change in net worth is

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.A: training, supervision, incentives and proper tools
questions.B: reducing the wages paid to the workers
questions.C: longer working hours without any rest
questions.D: removing all the machinery from the farm

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.C: sell land to the farmers cheaply

questions.B: measurement and mapping of the farm and its features

questions.D: sale of the farm produce in the market
questions.explanation: Surveys are needed for planning layouts, fencing, irrigation and settling boundary disputes.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a simple surveying equipment used on the farm?
questions.explanation: Others include pegs, arrows, cross staff, prismatic compass, offset staff and the field notebook.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Ranging poles are used in surveying to
questions.B: mark stations and keep survey lines straight
questions.C: dig holes for the boundary pegs
questions.D: measure the area of the field directly
questions.explanation: The red-and-white poles are sighted to align the chain.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The instrument used in chain surveying to set out perpendicular offsets is the
questions.explanation: Offsets locate features such as trees, huts and streams from the chain line.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Farmstead planning refers to
questions.A: the arrangement of buildings, roads and water points
questions.B: the ploughing of the land before planting
questions.C: the choice of the crop to be grown
questions.D: the vaccination of livestock against disease
questions.explanation: Good planning saves labour, improves hygiene and allows for expansion.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following factors should be considered when siting farm buildings?
questions.A: the colour of the roofing sheets only
questions.B: topography, drainage, access, water and wind direction
questions.C: the age of the farmer and his family
questions.D: the number of cows on the farm only
questions.explanation: Buildings should be on well-drained, slightly elevated ground with easy access.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A farm road is important because it
questions.B: eases movement of inputs, produce and machinery
questions.C: keeps the animals inside the farm
questions.D: prevents rain from falling on the crops
questions.explanation: Roads should link all buildings and fields and be well drained.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: In farmstead planning, livestock houses should be located
questions.A: inside the farmer's own dwelling house
questions.B: some distance from the dwelling, downwind of it
questions.C: on the flood plain close to the river
questions.D: beside the well, upstream of the house
questions.explanation: Manure should also be stored away from water sources.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The field notebook in surveying is used to
questions.B: store the seeds for the next season
questions.C: list the diseases of the animals
questions.D: record the prices of produce in the market
questions.explanation: Measurements are recorded from the bottom of the page upwards, in the direction of chaining.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Fencing of farm land serves to
questions.B: mark boundaries and keep animals in or out
questions.C: increase the erosion of the topsoil
questions.D: block sunlight from reaching the crops
questions.explanation: Fences may be live hedges, barbed wire, wooden posts or electric.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The simple farm tool used for clearing bush and cutting grass is the
questions.explanation: The cutlass is the commonest tool on West African farms.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The hoe is used mainly for
questions.explanation: The West African hoe has a broad blade set at an acute angle to a short handle.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The tool used for collecting cut grass, leaves and rubbish and for levelling seedbeds is the
questions.explanation: Rakes have a row of teeth on a long handle.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The curved-bladed hand tool used for harvesting rice and cutting grass is the
questions.explanation: The sickle's serrated or sharp curved blade cuts stalks close to the ground.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Secateurs are used for
questions.B: pruning small branches and cutting stems
questions.explanation: Larger branches need a pruning saw or shears.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A hand trowel is used for
questions.A: felling large trees in the forest
questions.B: transplanting seedlings and lifting small plants
questions.C: harvesting yam tubers from the mounds
questions.explanation: Its small scoop-shaped blade lifts seedlings with soil around the roots.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The go-to-hell (Gothel) or digger is used for
questions.B: digging holes for posts and deep-rooted crops
questions.C: harvesting maize cobs from the stalks
questions.D: pruning the branches of fruit trees
questions.explanation: The long-handled chisel-bladed tool digs post holes and harvests yams and cassava.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Simple farm tools should be maintained by
questions.A: leaving them out in the rain after use
questions.B: cleaning, sharpening, oiling and storing them dry
questions.C: burying them in the soil after each use
questions.D: painting the cutting edges with oil paint
questions.explanation: Loose handles should be tightened and wooden handles kept from cracking.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The watering can is used to
questions.A: measure the rainfall on the farm
questions.B: apply water gently to seedlings in the nursery
questions.D: carry harvested crops to the store
questions.explanation: The perforated rose breaks the water into fine drops that do not wash out seeds.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The knapsack sprayer is used for
questions.A: watering the plants in the nursery
questions.B: applying pesticides and herbicides as fine spray
questions.D: pruning the branches of fruit trees
questions.explanation: It is carried on the back and pumped by hand; protective clothing must be worn.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A farmer's cutlass rusts quickly and its handle keeps coming loose. The best corrective practice is to
questions.A: buy a new cutlass at the end of each week
questions.B: clean and oil the blade, store it dry and fix the handle
questions.C: leave the cutlass in the soil after use
questions.D: sharpen the cutlass once every year
questions.explanation: Routine maintenance extends tool life and improves safety.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following tools is used for turning the soil and digging trenches?
questions.explanation: The spade has a flat blade for digging; the shovel has a curved blade for lifting loose material.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The most important source of power on a mechanised farm is the
questions.explanation: Tractors provide power for tillage, planting, spraying, harvesting and transport.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The implement attached to a tractor for primary tillage is the
questions.explanation: Disc and mouldboard ploughs cut and invert the soil.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The machine that cuts, threshes and cleans grain in one operation is the
questions.explanation: Combines are used for rice, wheat, maize and sorghum on large farms.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The device on a tractor that provides rotary power to implements such as sprayers and mowers is the
questions.explanation: The PTO transmits engine power to attached machinery.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is an advantage of farm mechanisation?
questions.A: increased drudgery for the farm workers
questions.B: timely operations and increased output per worker
questions.C: automatic increase in the fertility of the soil
questions.D: a reduction in the land under cultivation
questions.explanation: Machines enable large areas to be cultivated quickly.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A major problem of mechanisation in West Africa is
questions.B: small fragmented holdings and costly machines
questions.C: land that is too flat for machines
questions.D: abundant capital in the hands of farmers
questions.explanation: Tree stumps, tsetse-free zones for draught animals and poor maintenance culture also limit mechanisation.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Animal (draught) power is used in the northern savanna of Nigeria mainly because
questions.A: the area is covered with thick forest
questions.B: the zone is tsetse-free and cattle are abundant
questions.C: tractors are given free to the farmers
questions.D: the soils of the zone are very rocky
questions.explanation: Oxen pull ploughs, ridgers and carts; the forest zone is unsuitable because of trypanosomiasis.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The tractor implement used to break clods and prepare a fine seedbed after ploughing is the
questions.explanation: Disc harrows pulverise and level the ploughed soil.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a source of farm power?
questions.A: human, animal, mechanical and solar power
questions.D: improved seed sown on the farm
questions.explanation: Human power is the commonest in West Africa; solar power is increasingly used for pumps.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Routine maintenance of a tractor includes
questions.A: changing the colour of the body
questions.B: checking oil, water, tyre pressure and fuel daily
questions.C: removing the brakes to save weight
questions.D: running the engine without any oil
questions.explanation: Preventive maintenance reduces breakdowns and extends machine life.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A tractor ploughs 1.5 hectares per hour. The time required to plough a 30-hectare farm, if it works 8 hours a day, is

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The implement used to make ridges after harrowing is the
questions.explanation: Ridgers have two mouldboards that throw soil to both sides.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A precision planter is used to
questions.A: spray the weeds between the rows
questions.B: place seeds at uniform depth and spacing
questions.C: harvest the crops at the end of the season
questions.D: make hay from the cut grass
questions.explanation: Planters may also apply fertiliser at the same time.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The main disadvantage of the tractor over draught animals for a small farmer is
questions.A: the tractor works more slowly than oxen
questions.B: the high purchase, fuel and maintenance costs
questions.C: the tractor needs pasture for grazing
questions.D: the tractor cannot plough heavy soils
questions.explanation: Tractor hiring services and cooperatives help small farmers use machinery.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Cassava is processed into garri in order to
questions.A: increase the water content of the tubers
questions.B: remove the cyanide, preserve it and add value
questions.C: make the tubers heavier for sale
questions.D: make the tubers easier to plant
questions.explanation: Grating, fermenting, pressing and frying remove hydrocyanic acid and give a storable product.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Grains should be dried to a moisture content of about
questions.explanation: High moisture allows moulds and insects to thrive in storage.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The traditional structure used in northern Nigeria for storing grain is the
questions.explanation: The rhombus is built of mud with a thatched roof and raised on stones.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Yams are traditionally stored in
questions.A: metal silos raised above the ground
questions.B: barns, tied to vertical poles in the shade
questions.explanation: Ventilation and shade reduce rotting and sprouting.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The maize crib is used to
questions.B: store maize cobs with good air circulation
questions.C: plant the maize seed in rows
questions.D: shell the grains from the cobs
questions.explanation: Cribs are raised on stilts with rat guards.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is a method of preserving meat and fish?
questions.A: leaving it uncovered in the sun
questions.D: wrapping it in fresh leaves only
questions.explanation: Preservation methods inhibit microbial growth.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Pasteurisation of milk involves
questions.A: boiling the milk for one full hour
questions.B: heating to about 72 °C for 15 seconds, then cooling
questions.D: adding sugar and salt to the milk
questions.explanation: Pasteurisation kills disease organisms without greatly changing flavour.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Cold storage preserves perishable produce by
questions.A: killing all the organisms in the produce
questions.B: slowing microbial and enzyme activity when cold
questions.C: removing all the water from the produce
questions.explanation: Refrigeration (0–4 °C) and freezing (−18 °C) are used for meat, fish, milk and vegetables.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Fumigation of stored grain with phostoxin tablets is done to
questions.A: improve the flavour of the grain
questions.B: kill insect pests in airtight stores
questions.D: increase the moisture of the grain
questions.explanation: Fumigants are dangerous and must be used by trained persons in sealed stores.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Post-harvest losses of fruits and vegetables in Nigeria are high because of
questions.A: the excellent cold chains in the country
questions.B: perishability, poor handling and lack of storage
questions.C: too much processing of the produce
questions.D: the low production of the crops
questions.explanation: Losses of tomatoes can exceed 40% between farm and market.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Threshing is the
questions.B: separation of grain from the stalk or cob
questions.explanation: Winnowing then separates the grain from the chaff.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Palm oil is extracted from the
questions.explanation: Palm kernel oil comes from the seed inside the nut.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Processing adds value to farm produce by
questions.A: reducing the shelf life of the produce
questions.B: converting it into durable or higher-priced forms
questions.C: making the produce heavier to carry
questions.D: removing the nutrients from the produce
questions.explanation: Examples: cassava to garri, milk to cheese, tomatoes to paste, groundnut to oil and cake.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Storage of farm produce is important because it
questions.A: increases the spoilage of the produce
questions.B: makes produce available all year at better prices
questions.C: automatically reduces the quality of produce
questions.D: prevents the processing of the produce
questions.explanation: Storage gives time utility and evens out seasonal price fluctuations.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Biotechnology in agriculture refers to
questions.A: the use of tractors and combine harvesters
questions.B: the use of living organisms to make or modify products
questions.C: the study of rocks and soil formation
questions.D: the keeping of accounts on the farm
questions.explanation: Tissue culture, genetic engineering, fermentation and biofertilisers are examples.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Tissue culture is used to
questions.A: produce many disease-free plants from small tissues
questions.explanation: Banana, plantain, cassava and pineapple are multiplied by tissue culture.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: A genetically modified (GM) crop is one
questions.A: grown without any fertiliser at all
questions.B: carrying genes inserted from another organism
questions.C: grown only in a glass greenhouse
questions.D: produced by grafting onto a rootstock
questions.explanation: Bt cotton and Bt cowpea (PBR cowpea, released in Nigeria in 2019) carry a bacterial gene for insect resistance.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Which of the following is an application of biotechnology in animal production?
questions.explanation: Cloning and genetic testing are further applications.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: One concern about GM crops is
questions.B: possible effects on health and the environment
questions.D: the reduced use of pesticides on them
questions.explanation: Biosafety regulation (NBMA in Nigeria) addresses these concerns.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: ICT can help farmers by
questions.A: increasing the price of farm inputs
questions.B: providing market prices and advice by mobile phone
questions.C: replacing all the labour on the farm
questions.explanation: SMS price alerts and e-wallet input schemes have been used in Nigeria.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The Growth Enhancement Support (GES) scheme in Nigeria used mobile phones to
questions.B: deliver subsidised input vouchers (e-wallet) to farmers
questions.C: vaccinate the animals of the farmers
questions.D: predict earthquakes in the farming areas
questions.explanation: The e-wallet reduced diversion of subsidised inputs by middlemen.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and remote sensing are used in agriculture to
questions.A: map soils, monitor crops and plan land use
questions.B: milk the cows on a dairy farm
questions.C: prune the trees in the orchard
questions.D: cook the food for the farm workers
questions.explanation: Satellite images detect drought stress, pest outbreaks and flooding.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Agricultural research is important because it
questions.A: increases the problems of the farmers
questions.B: develops improved varieties, breeds and practices
questions.C: replaces the farmers on the land
questions.D: reduces the yields of the crops
questions.explanation: Research institutes and universities of agriculture generate technologies passed on by extension.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science

questions.explanation: The control provides a baseline against which treatments are compared.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Replication in a field experiment means
questions.A: applying the same treatment to several plots
questions.explanation: Replication reduces the effect of chance variation and allows statistical analysis.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Randomisation in experimental design is used to
questions.A: give every treatment an equal chance of any plot
questions.B: choose the best plot for the favourite treatment
questions.C: reduce the number of plots in the trial
questions.D: increase the fertility of the soil in the trial
questions.explanation: Randomised complete block design is common in agronomy trials.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: The most suitable diagram for showing the yield of five maize varieties side by side is a
questions.explanation: Bars of proportional height make comparison of discrete categories easy.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Biofertilisers such as Rhizobium inoculants are used to
questions.A: kill the insects on the crop
questions.explanation: Inoculating soya bean seed with the right Rhizobium strain raises yields on new land.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Precision agriculture uses
questions.A: hoes and cutlasses for all operations
questions.B: GPS, sensors and data to apply inputs precisely
questions.C: bush burning to clear the land each year
questions.D: nomadic herding of cattle across zones
questions.explanation: Variable-rate application saves fertiliser and reduces pollution.

questions.subject: Agricultural Science
questions.q: Drones (UAVs) are used in modern agriculture for
questions.A: cooking food for the farm workers
questions.C: milking the cows on the dairy farm
questions.explanation: Drone imagery detects stress, pests and nutrient deficiency early.
